slides.title:
Find defective parts
before they ship
slides.body:
Use real circuit-board photos to compare detectors, review their mistakes, and save a version another engineer can reproduce.
Four hours · CPU classifiers · your own Forge project
slides.notes:
The inspection team is fictional. The VisA PCB1 images, masks and recorded comparisons are real. Do not promise that every participant run improves.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.name: opening
slides.concept: Find defective parts before they ship

slides.title: The factory has two ways to waste a good morning
slides.body:
A defect gets through

A board with a missing or damaged component passes inspection.

A good board gets held

An inspector spends time checking a normal board that the detector rejected.

Management has requested fewer of both. It has not supplied a third category called “probably fine.”
slides.notes:
Ask participants which cost matters in their own work. We will count both errors. The joke does not define the release threshold.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.

slides.concept: The factory has two ways to waste a good morning

slides.title: Start with the boards, not the score
slides.body:
Training example A

Training example B

VisA PCB1 · real photographs · labels hidden for this first inspection
slides.notes:
Ask learners to identify a region they would inspect. Do not infer a defect type without checking the supplied mask. They will reveal masks in the notebook. The same fitting example is bundled in the notebook setup. Ask for a pass/review choice before revealing its annotation; no authentication or download is needed.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.

slides.name: board-target
slides.title: Predict a label for the whole board
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="data" :step="1" />
slides.notes:
Ask participants to choose pass or inspection before advancing. The first figure hides its source label and mask. Identify the photograph as the input and the binary label as the target. A detector flags a board; it does not learn pixel labels here.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.

slides.name: mask-boundary
slides.title: Use the mask to investigate the decision
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="data" :step="2" />
slides.notes:
Now reveal pcb1-anomaly-005 from the fitting partition: source image pcb1/Data/Images/Anomaly/005.JPG, SHA-256 ec34541be729af29a287bde12d4e3955cf3f83c734baea8a9505a7b801ce54e2, VisA CC BY 4.0. Source metadata and bundled image/mask checksums are in decks/inspection/data/feature-example.json. Ask which input would leak the answer if passed to the classifier. The mask is reference evidence for human inspection; neither masks nor test labels enter feature assembly.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.concept: Use the mask to investigate the decision

slides.title: What is in the teaching set?
slides.body:
1,104 photographs

One PCB family. 1,004 normal boards and 100 defective boards.

Image labels

A board-level normal or defective label is the classifier target.

Defect masks

Annotations let us inspect mistakes. They never enter the classifier.

VisA, Zou et al. · CC BY 4.0 · the provided supervised split is preserved
slides.notes:
Explain the distinction between detecting a defective board and locating its defect. This classifier does the former. A patch-distance heatmap is not a segmentation model.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.

slides.title: Connect to your own experiment
slides.body:
Open the Visual Inspection notebook and copy it into your Forge project.
  1. Confirm Your Forge entity/project.
  2. Click Connect and restore my inspection work.
  3. Edit the attribute in instrument_inspection_tool, then click Send my first inspection trace.
Check: Find your attribute and the returned NumPy version in Agent Lens.
slides.notes:
Hosted authentication comes from the copied notebook. A laptop uses uv run wandb login. The core path has no inference calls; notebook compute remains separately billed.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.

slides.title: Inspect one board before revealing its label
slides.body:
Notebook step: Inspect the boards.
  1. Click Download and verify the PCB1 teaching data.
  2. Choose a training board. Explain what would make you inspect it.
  3. Turn on Reveal the published defect label and mask.
Check: Describe the annotated region without treating the mask as an input to your detector.

This is a participant decision, not a model evaluation. Give people a minute to make their own assessment before discussion.

slides.title: Reuse a fixed image encoder
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="encoder" :step="1" />
slides.notes:
The ImageNet encoder is fixed. Fitting our logistic classifier changes its weights but not ResNet-18. The small cache can be reused in a CPU notebook.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.name: encoder
slides.concept: Reuse a fixed image encoder

slides.title: Fit a first detector on whole-image features
slides.body:
```python {1-4|6|all} model = inspection.fit_classifier( data, fit_rows, method, build_features=build_features, C=0.03, ) validation_scores = inspection.score( data, validation_rows, model, build_features=build_features, ) ```
C controls regularization. This worked recipe fixes C before your run; labels and training cases are the same.
slides.notes:
Do not describe this as training a vision foundation model. We fit a logistic classifier over fixed encoder outputs. Patch distances add features but do not use pixel masks.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.name: classifier
slides.concept: Fit a first detector on whole-image features

slides.name: fit-operation
slides.title: Fit on training boards; measure on validation boards
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="train" :step="1" />
slides.notes:
Point to the learner build_features argument. The same function must be supplied to fit and score. We fit a small class-balanced logistic classifier, not the ResNet encoder. Saving a completed fit and exporting its trace happen afterward.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.concept: Fit on training boards; measure on validation boards

slides.title: A detector score still needs an operating rule
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="threshold" :step="1" />
slides.notes:
Scores are decision values, not calibrated defect probabilities. The optional review margin is in score units. A valid threshold function does not make the policy safe.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.name: threshold
slides.concept: A detector score still needs an operating rule

slides.name: validation-cutoff
slides.title: Require 11 of the 12 validation defects to be caught
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="threshold" :step="2" />
slides.notes:
The slider uses the exact existing free fixture. With three fixture defects and recall 2/3 the cutoff is 0.7. For the real validation set, ceil(.9*12)=11. Explain that the chosen cutoff constrains this validation set only.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.concept: Require 11 of the 12 validation defects to be caught

slides.title: Implement the validation threshold
slides.body:
Notebook step: Train the whole-image baseline.
  1. In choose_threshold, sort the scores of known validation defects.
  2. Choose the largest cutoff that still catches at least 90% of them.
  3. Click Check my threshold function, then Train the whole-image baseline.
Check: Open one validation miss or false alarm before adding patch features.
slides.notes:
Allow participants to finish the local check before training. The 90 percent requirement constrains recall on validation only, not a guarantee for the final set.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.name: threshold-exercise
slides.concept: Implement the validation threshold

slides.name: baseline-observation
slides.title: Inspect a baseline miss or false alarm
slides.body:
Notebook: Train the whole-image baseline
  1. Select a validation board. Compare the photograph, annotation, score, and cutoff.
  2. Explain what the whole-image detector missed or flagged. What local detail might help?
  3. Optionally click Save my baseline observation.

Check: A saved baseline decision supports your hypothesis. No patch model has run yet.
slides.notes:
Choose a saved validation error if available; do not force a failure. If the baseline gets the selected board right, describe what evidence would distinguish the next representation. The displayed score comes from the saved weights and feature source.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/scripts/inspection_cells.py.
slides.concept: Inspect a baseline miss or false alarm

slides.name: patch-grid
slides.title: Keep local information as well as the whole image
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="encoder" :step="2" />
slides.notes:
Read the shapes out loud: N boards, 14 rows, 14 columns, 64 feature channels. The overlay shows feature positions schematically, not exact independent image crops. The whole-image representation has 512 values; the grid retains spatial differences.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.concept: Keep local information as well as the whole image

slides.title: Compare local features at the same board position
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="patch" :step="1" />
slides.notes:
Use only normal fitting boards as the reference bank. At each spatial position, find the closest actual reference vector after scaling. A normal fitting board cannot match itself. The older mean-patch result is preserved beside the later recorded comparison.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.name: patches
slides.concept: Compare each patch with real normal examples

slides.name: one-patch-distance
slides.title: Calculate the distance at one image position
slides.body:
Notebook: Compute image features

Click Calculate one patch distance. Read the visible calculation at row 7, column 7 of fitting board pcb1-anomaly-005.

  1. Scale each channel using normal fitting boards.
  2. Compare the query vector with each normal vector at that position.
  3. Take the smallest mean squared difference, then log1p.

Check: Your displayed minimum agrees with nearest_patch_errors.
slides.notes:
These values come from the real prepared feature cache, not the five-board threshold fixture. Only fitting boards form the reference bank. The free calculation does not fit a classifier.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/scripts/inspection_cells.py.
slides.concept: Calculate the distance at one image position

slides.name: append-patches
slides.title: Append 196 distances to the 512 whole-image values
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="features" :step="2" />
slides.notes:
Walk the same board through errors, log1p, reshape and concatenate. The output has 708 columns. axis=0 would add observations rather than features and fail the shape/order fixture. log1p compresses large distances; it does not turn them into probabilities.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.concept: Append 196 distances to the 512 whole-image values

slides.title: Add local information to the classifier
slides.body:
Notebook step: Compute image features.
  1. Complete build_features: calculate patch errors, apply np.log1p, and flatten one row per board.
  2. Append the patch values to the whole-image vector along axis 1.
  3. Click Check my patch-feature function.
Check: The check preserves board order and verifies both whole-image and nearest-patch behavior.
slides.notes:
The learner function is passed into fitting and saved with the freeze. Final evaluation reloads that saved source, not the current draft.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.name: features
slides.concept: Add local information to the classifier

slides.title: Check the feature cache without rebuilding everything
slides.body:
```python weights = teaching.fetch_weights(weights_path) result = teaching.recompute_batch(data_root, weights) assert result["matching_cached_features"] ```
Optional button: Recompute four cached board features. Downloads pinned weights; no model-provider call.
slides.notes:
The retained lossless inputs allow exact feature comparison. The prepared full cache took 39.25 seconds on the preparation Mac using two Torch CPU threads. This is not an attendee timing guarantee.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.name: cache
slides.concept: Check the feature cache without rebuilding everything

slides.name: patch-experiment
slides.title: Test patches against the saved baseline
slides.body:
Notebook: Compare global and patch features
  1. Keep the whole-image branch, C=0.03, and threshold rule unchanged.
  2. Click Train the patch-feature alternative.
  3. Compare its validation mistakes with the saved whole-image result.

Check: Both representations are saved before continuing to review selection.
slides.notes:
The first fit remains valid while learners implement the patch branch. A changed threshold rule or changed whole-image inputs would confound this comparison and is rejected. Previously saved matching runs are reused.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/scripts/inspection_cells.py.
slides.concept: Test patches against the saved baseline

slides.title: Keep ranking quality and operating errors separate
slides.body:
MeasureQuestion it answers
Average precisionAre defective boards ranked ahead of normal boards?
Misses and false alarmsWhat happens at the frozen threshold?
Review volumeHow many decisions are handed to a person?
slides.notes:
AP summarizes precision over recall levels. Do not compare it to accuracy or confuse a change in review volume with better detection.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.name: metrics
slides.concept: Keep ranking quality and operating errors separate

slides.name: ranking-ap
slides.title: Calculate ranking quality before choosing one cutoff
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="ranking" :step="1" />
slides.notes:
Use the five public fixture scores. Defects occur at ranks 2,3,4; precision is 1/2,2/3,3/4 at those recalls. Average precision is their mean, 0.638889. This is an illustrative calculation, not a PCB1 result.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.concept: Calculate ranking quality before choosing one cutoff

slides.name: operating-errors
slides.title: Count operating errors at the chosen cutoff
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="ranking" :step="2" />
slides.notes:
At cutoff 0.7, the fixture has one missed defect and one false alarm. Moving the cutoff leaves the score ordering and AP unchanged. A review band sends additional cases to people and should be reported as workload, not detection improvement.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.
slides.concept: Count operating errors at the chosen cutoff

slides.name: active-selection
slides.title: Choose uncertain boards before opening their labels
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="review" :step="1" />
slides.notes:
Predict which scores the selector will choose. The public fixture uses row IDs 10,20,30,40 with scores .8,-.1,.01,-.9. At threshold 0, the two closest rows are 20 and 30. The function receives no labels.

slides.name: random-control
slides.title: Give random selection the same labeling budget
slides.body: <InspectionMechanism kind="review" :step="2" />
slides.notes:
Both branches start from the same nearest-patch parent and review pool. Each gets 24 labels; overlapping selections are allowed across methods. Random selection controls for simply receiving more data. Do not promise that uncertainty sampling wins.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.

Notebook step: Choose examples to review.
  1. Complete choose_review using distance from the current threshold. Do not read labels.
  2. Click Check my review selector.
  3. Click Select 24 boards for each review method.
Check: The active and random methods select 24 cases each from the same pool.

The random condition matters because any additional labeled data might help. We cannot credit the selection strategy for the entire gain.

slides.title: Worked answer: meet the validation recall target
slides.body:
```python positives = np.sort(scores[target == 1])[::-1] position = int(np.ceil(recall * len(positives))) - 1 return float(positives[position]) ```
At 12 validation defects and recall .90, keep the top 11 above the threshold.
slides.notes:
The retained cutoff depends on validation examples. It does not guarantee the same recall on final boards.
Teaching source: https://github.com/ash0ts/forge-workshop-kit/blob/main/src/forge_workshop_kit/inspection.py.

slides.title: Worked answer: choose uncertain cases
slides.body:
```python rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) order = rng.permutation(len(rows)) order = order[np.argsort( np.abs(scores[order] - threshold), kind="stable" )] return np.asarray(rows)[order[:budget]] ```
The permutation only breaks equal-distance ties. Do not pass labels to this function.
slides.notes:
Active selection here is uncertainty sampling. It is one policy to test, not a proven universal choice.
